 Welcome to the Dubuque County Elections website. The

 is a division of the

 upcoming elections, how to vote, finding your elected officials, getting involved with elections,
 and more.

 General Election
 
 
 
County wide Election with polls open from 7:00am to 8:00pm on November 3rd. This election is to fill Federal, State and County offices.

Extended Office HoursMonday October 19th 8:00 am to 5:00 pm
Wednesday, October 21st 6:00 am to 4:30 pm
Saturday October 24th 8:00 am to 3:00 pm

Dates & Deadlines 

 
 October 14, 2026
First Day to vote in-person at the Election Office for the November 3, 2026 General Election.Satellite VotingCascade City Hall, 320 1st Ave W, from 9:00 am to 3:00 pm on October 15th.
Loras College 4th Floor Mezzanine outside The Campus Center Ballroom 1450 Alta Vista St, from 9:00 am to 3:00 pm On October 21st.
Dyersrville Social Center, 625 3rd Ave SE, from 7:30 am to 1:30 pm, on October 24th.



 



 

 More Dates

To learn more about where to vote on 
 Election Day, visit our 
 Where to 
 Vote page. If you are unable to use the application above to determine your polling location, call the Dubuque County Elections office at (563) 589-4457 or visit the Iowa Secretary of State's 
 Find Your Polling Place Search.

Absentee Ballot Request Form
 
 

 Starting 70 days before Election Day, the Elections Office accepts
 
 Absentee Ballot Request Forms .
 To receive an Absentee Ballot in the mail, the Elections Office must receive your
 completed Absentee Ballot Request Form by 5pm on the Monday, 15 days before Election Day.
 

 
 

 Don't have a printer? Complete our
 online form and Dubuque County Elections will send you a
 printed
 Absentee Ballot Request Form in the mail.
 
 
 
 
 

 
FAQ?
 
 Q. Will the county Elections Office send absentee ballot request forms to all voters in the county?
 
A. No. State law now prohibits this. If you personally request an absentee ballot request form, the Elections Office will send you one. Please visit our Absentee Voting page to learn more.

 Q. What if I don’t have a four-digit Pin number?
 
A. When filling out an Absentee Ballot Request form this is an OR question. If
 you have an Iowa Driver’s License or Non-Operator ID number you should use this number as your ID number
 on the request form, as you are not automatically mailed a voter Pin card. However, any voter may
 request an Iowa Voter Identification Card.

 always looking for community-minded citizens ready to roll up their sleeves and help make a
 difference by working at the polls on Election Day.
